blocks.content: Let's see a few different types of exceptions.
This exception can occur in many circumstances. One of the conditions in which it occurs is when we divide a number by zero. For example,
When we divide a number by zero, the result is undefined. So, we get a Floating point exception.
This exception occurs when we use dynamic memory allocation to allocate an extremely large number of memory blocks to an array.
In other words, this exception occurs when the array size is far too large for the computer to handle. For example,

terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
what():  std::bad_alloc
Aborted

Here, the size of the dynamically created array is 10000000000000000. However, the computer does not possess the memory required to store such an array. Hence, we get a Bad Allocation exception, which is indicated by the code std::bad_alloc.
Now that we know about exceptions, we will learn to handle exceptions in the next lesson.
